name: Little India
summary: NEL/DTL cultural belt north of Rochor — spice markets, late kitchens, and mixed condo/walk-up stock with festival and weekend crowd taxes.
body: Little India is the shortlist when North-East / Downtown Line access and Serangoon Road food density matter more than polished Orchard living. Housing mixes older walk-ups, boutique condos, and estate edges toward Rochor / Farrer Park; Deepavali and weekend market crowds are the tax. Expats land here for car-light CBD hops, vegetarian / Indian-Muslim food gravity, and rents below River Valley. Compare with Rochor for a slightly tighter DTL interchange feel, Jalan Besar for late-kitchen energy without the deepest tourist crush, and Farrer Park when you want a calmer residential edge one stop away.
bestFor: car-light workers who want NEL/DTL optionality
households who cook less and walk to food belts
renters okay with festival and weekend footfall
people who will book ActiveSG indoor courts instead of trusting condo halls
housingMix: Older walk-ups, boutique condos, and estate edges toward Rochor / Farrer Park.
commuteNotes: North-East and Downtown Line access via Little India / Rochor / Farrer Park cluster; test a Sunday market-hour walk and a Tuesday 08:15 door-to-desk.
